executive_summary: US stock futures are pulling back 0.3-0.4% overnight as the US-Iran ceasefire narrative unravels less than 24 hours after announcement. Iran's Parliament Speaker claims three clauses have been breached, the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked with 800+ vessels stranded, and WTI crude is rebounding toward $97/bbl after yesterday's 15% crash. The FOMC March minutes released yesterday confirmed a higher-for-longer rate stance at 3.50-3.75% with only one cut projected this year. Tomorrow's March CPI release will be the next major catalyst. The AI/semiconductor sector continues to provide structural support — Samsung's Q1 profit surged 700% on HBM demand, Intel jumped on the Musk Terafab announcement, and Broadcom secured a long-term custom chip deal with Google.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Collapse — Strait of Hormuz Remains Blocked
macro_events.causal_chain: Trump announced 2-week ceasefire April 7 → markets surged (Dow +1,300, oil -15%) → Iran claims 3 clauses breached within 24 hours (Israeli strikes on Lebanon continue) → Strait of Hormuz remains blocked → 800+ ships stranded, 20% of global daily oil supply disrupted → tanker war-risk insurance premiums spike → Asian refiners forced to reroute via Omani coastline (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip per VLCC) → Qatar LNG to Europe at risk → Brent/WTI rebounding to $97 → airlines face higher fuel costs → consumer inflation expectations rise → Fed's rate cut timeline pushed further out
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Persian Gulf, global energy supply chains, European gas markets, Asian refining hubs
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent surged 15% in 24 hours, tanker rates jumped 20-35% in one week. Current disruption is broader given full Hormuz closure vs single facility attack.
macro_events.counterargument: Trump has strong incentive to enforce ceasefire and reopen Hormuz before domestic fuel prices spike further. Diplomatic back-channels may produce de-escalation faster than market expects. Alternative Omani routing is already functioning.

macro_events.title: FOMC March Minutes — Higher-for-Longer Confirmed, One Cut in 2026
macro_events.causal_chain: FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% → dot plot shows only one cut this year, one in 2027 → Governor Miran dissented for a cut (dovish minority growing) → Powell emphasized 'no cuts without further inflation improvement' → tariff-driven inflation stalling progress → PCE expected at 2.7% (above 2% target) → Middle East oil shock adds upside inflation risk → market repricing rate expectations → 10Y yield elevated near 4.31% → mortgage rates +40bps from early-year lows → housing sector pressure → growth-sensitive sectors face higher discount rates
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic monetary policy with global spillovers to EM currencies and sovereign debt
macro_events.historical_analog: 2023 higher-for-longer cycle — 10Y yield peaked at 5% in October 2023, causing 10% S&P drawdown. Current setup is less extreme but same directional risk.
macro_events.counterargument: Miran's dissent signals growing internal pressure to cut. If ceasefire holds and oil drops, inflation picture improves rapidly. Labor market softening (low job gains noted) could force the Fed's hand.

affected_tickers.reason: Higher-for-longer means duration pain; 10Y yields likely test 4.40%+

macro_events.title: March CPI Release Tomorrow — Positioning Day
macro_events.causal_chain: March CPI scheduled April 10 at 8:30 AM ET → February CPI was +0.3% MoM, 2.4% YoY → tariff pass-through and elevated energy prices expected to push March reading higher → if CPI surprises hot (>0.4% MoM), rate cut expectations collapse → 10Y yield spikes → growth stocks sell off → if CPI comes in cool (<0.2%), relief rally resumes → today is positioning day — expect reduced risk appetite and gamma hedging into the print
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US consumer economy, imported goods inflation from tariffs, energy cost pass-through
macro_events.historical_analog: January 2024 hot CPI print — S&P dropped 1.4% on the day, 10Y yield jumped 14bps. Market is similarly positioned for a directional move.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI may have moderated as shelter inflation eases. Base effects from prior year make YoY comparisons more favorable. Market may already be pricing in a hot print given geopolitical uncertainty.

affected_tickers.reason: Hot CPI = higher discount rates = tech multiple compression

macro_events.title: AI/Semiconductor Capex Supercycle Accelerates
macro_events.causal_chain: Samsung Q1 profit +700% on HBM demand → industry projected to spend $1.3T on semiconductors in 2026 (+64% YoY) → Intel joins Musk Terafab project (SpaceX/Tesla/xAI consortium) → Broadcom secures long-term Google custom chip deal + Anthropic expansion → Oracle finances $14B Michigan AI data center via PIMCO → Nvidia-backed Firmus hits $5.5B valuation → BUT ASML falls on MATCH Act (tighter China export controls, ~low teens % of 2026 revenue at risk) → Supermicro investigation over alleged $2.5B Nvidia chip smuggling → supply chain integrity concerns rising
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-China semiconductor decoupling, US domestic fab buildout, Korean memory competition (Samsung vs SK Hynix vs Micron)
macro_events.historical_analog: 2000 telecom capex cycle — massive infrastructure spending preceded by years, eventual overcapacity. Current AI cycle is earlier stage with real revenue traction (Broadcom AI rev +106% YoY).
macro_events.counterargument: MATCH Act could constrain ASML and upstream equipment makers. Community resistance to data center power/water demands creates new permitting friction. Zhipu price increases (+8%) suggest subsidized growth phase ending.

macro_events.title: Export Control Escalation — MATCH Act and Supply Chain Integrity
macro_events.causal_chain: Proposed MATCH Act tightens restrictions on semiconductor equipment exports to China → ASML faces low-teens percentage revenue at risk in 2026 → Supermicro cofounder arrested over alleged $2.5B Nvidia chip smuggling to China → exposes compliance gaps in AI hardware supply chains → North Korean hackers deploying malicious packages across npm/PyPI → Iran-affiliated hackers exploiting PLCs in US critical infrastructure → cascading security concerns raise costs for AI supply chain participants
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-China tech decoupling, EU semiconductor equipment sector (ASML), global cybersecurity
macro_events.historical_analog: 2022 CHIPS Act and October 2022 export controls — ASML dropped 30% in Q4 2022 on China revenue fears before recovering. Current situation is incremental tightening.
macro_events.counterargument: MATCH Act is still proposed, not enacted. ASML has diversified customer base. China is developing domestic alternatives (SMIC 5nm process) which creates demand pull for non-restricted equipment.
